values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/arbutuslake ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground', 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: The DNR gives 24 sites: 12 'small-to-medium sites for trailer use' and 11 tent-only sites reached by stairs (23 of the 24 accounted for). No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/arbutuslake ('There are 24 sites (12 are small-to-medium sites for trailer use and 11 are tent-only sites with stair access)', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Accessible boat launch.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/arbutuslake ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well', 'There is an accessible boat launch'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/arbutuslake ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay'), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic Michigan DNR state forest campground in hilly beech-maple hardwoods on the northwest shore of Arbutus Lake #4 (a chain of five small lakes), 10.6 miles southeast of Traverse City via US-31 and Three Mile Road. --Claude
summary: DNR page: 24 sites (12 small-to-medium trailer sites, 11 tent-only by stairs), $20/night at the kiosk + Recreation Passport (fees.note), no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, accessible boat launch; first-come only, 15-day maximum (max stay, previously inherited, now on the entry). Season (open all year) already manual. Phone matches. Note trimmed of what the fields hold.
flags: Rig fit (curation rule b, vague tier): the DNR singles this campground out with its own wording, '12 are small-to-medium sites for trailer use' (not the 'sites for tent and small trailer use' boilerplate), and posts no length. No review from the last 3 years reports a 23-ft+ rig fitting: the only RV review (Campendium, June 3, 2023, over 3 years old) says 'We got one of the last sites that would have fit our RV ... it would have been no problem. You might unhook if you're a class A towing a car' but gives no length; the September 2026 review says nothing about rigs. By the rule, a vague agency description with no qualifying review is a drop; a human should decide.
Waterfront re-audit lead: the DNR says the campground 'sits along the northwest shore of Arbutus Lake #4' and 'is located on Arbutus Lake'; the entry has 'not waterfront'.
